name: Sodium nitroprusside
executiveSummary: Immediate arterial/venous vasodilator. Adult: start **0.3–0.5 µg/kg/min**, usual titration **0.5–5 µg/kg/min** (max **10 µg/kg/min**). Pediatrics: start **0.3–1 µg/kg/min**, maintenance often ≤**4–6 µg/kg/min**. Protect from light; cyanide/thiocyanate risk.
indications:
## Indications

- Hypertensive emergency with organ injury when immediate control is needed.
- Afterload reduction in acute heart failure / cardiac surgery per protocol.

## Precautions

- **Cyanide toxicity** (high dose, >24–48 h, liver failure) and **thiocyanate** (renal failure, prolonged use).
- Protect bag and line from light; discard if blue/gray/dark.
- Prefer **D5W**. Central line preferred. Invasive BP recommended.

> Use lowest dose and shortest time; consider alternatives (nicardipine, labetalol, NTG).

adulto.dose: Start **0.3–0.5 µg/kg/min**; titrate every few minutes. Usual range **0.5–5 µg/kg/min**; ceiling **10 µg/kg/min**. Avoid prolonged high doses.
adulto.administration: Continuous pump infusion; dilute in D5W (opaque/light-protected). Usual concentrations 50–200 µg/mL per card.
adulto.notes: Monitor BP, HR, lactate, toxicity signs (acidosis, confusion).

pediatrico.dose: Start **0.5–1 µg/kg/min**; usual maintenance up to **4–6 µg/kg/min** (institutional max often **10 µg/kg/min** briefly).
pediatrico.administration: Pump only; **D5W only**. Usual conc. **200 µg/mL**; fluid restriction up to **1000 µg/mL**.

stability:
## Stability

- Reconstituted/diluted: ~24 h if light-protected. Discard if discolored.
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Excessive hypotension, reflex tachycardia, headache, nausea; cyanide/thiocyanate toxicity; hypothyroidism with chronic thiocyanate.
